newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Gold revaluation in 1998 to boost Dutch reserves.
newsitem.headline: Gold revaluation in 1998 to boost Dutch reserves.

text.p: The next revaluation of the Dutch central bank's gold reserves at the end of 1998 will increase the value of the bank's reserves by some five to six billion guilders, Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said on Tuesday.
Dutch news agency ANP, reporting the minister's comments to parliament, said Zalm had made clear there were no plans to use the revaluation to lower the Netherlands' budget deficit.

Zalm recently hit out at Germany's controversial plan to use a revaluation of its gold reserves to lower its budget deficit so that it can meet the European monetary union (EMU) target figure of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Earlier this month the Dutch central bank said it would continue its policy of revaluing its gold reserves every three years at average market prices for the previous three years, less 30 percent.
The bank said at the time it had 1,061 tonnes of gold in reserve which were valued at 11.7 billion guilders.
In January 1997 the Dutch central bank said it had sold 300 tonnes of gold from its reserves in 1996, raising $3.8 billion which were added to its foreign curency reserves.
